text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGER: pg-1 GPU pool pressure alert for GPU pool 'hotpath-prod' — sustained queue depth > 120 requests for 3m, autoscaler failed to provision due to quota limit. Triggered at 2026-03-10T20:12:34Z.
Maya: seeing the queue spike in the dashboard, latency jumps to 450ms p95. autoscaler logs show repeated allocation errors.
Anil: copying relevant autoscaler error: `failed to create node: quota_exceeded: requested 8 GPUs, remaining 0` — looks like quota cap for the org hit.
Sam: @Maya @Anil oncall is me, I'm taking this. Quick assessment: are we seeing driver errors or just capacity shortage?
Maya: both. driver error rate (XID 40/43) increased on a subset of nodes in the pool around the same time. nodes flit in/out causing capacity to appear available then not.
Priya: adding logs snippet from node gpu-12: ```kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 43, PID 3456, GPU 0: 0x00000000```. seen repeated OOMs in container logs right before node dropped.
OpsBot: autoscaler: attempted scale-up -> API error `403 Quota exhausted` (project quota=32gpus, used=32gpus).
Sam: OK two parallel issues: (1) effective capacity shrink due to driver/runtime instability on ~5 nodes; (2) cannot scale due to org quota. Priorities: triage driver instability to stabilize capacity, request emergency quota bump, and put temporary traffic shaping in front of hotpath.
Maya: I'm starting node diagnostic on the flapping hosts, pulling dmesg, nvidia-smi output. will paste results.
Anil: I'll open a quota request with cloud support now — setting it as emergency. ETA for quota increase? usually 20-40m if expedited.
Sam: In the meantime, let's reduce concurrency per instance for the hotpath route and enable fallback model variant to avoid cascade. Routing change: set max_concurrency=1 on route `/v1/generate/hot` and fallback to `hot-light` model. Lee, can you apply that?
Lee: applying now via console, patching route config: ```routes.hotpath.max_concurrency=1; routes.hotpath.fallback=redwood/hot-light:v2```. Pushing change... done. Please monitor error rates.
Priya: Node diag from gpu-12: `oom_kill: kill process 3456 (runtime) score 985` followed by `nvidia: GPU reset requested by driver`. Restart loops observed ~2x/min for this node.
Maya: Looks like a memory leak in the runtime process on those nodes under certain workload patterns — spike in persistent GPU mem usage then Xid 43 and reset. I'm collecting core dumps and a safe-config to repro.
Sam: Good. Ops mitigation: cordon the 5 flapping nodes from the hotpath pool so autoscaler doesn't try to schedule there while we debug. That frees up scheduling pressure. Maya, cordon them?
Maya: cordoned nodes gpu-11,gpu-12,gpu-19,gpu-20,gpu-21 from pool 'hotpath-prod'. Redirecting traffic off them.
Anil: quota request opened support ticket #CLD-82492 with expedited flag. cloud responded: can raise +8 gpus in 30-45m if we provide justification (pager + customer impact). Providing now.
Sam: Customer impact: we see 3 customer-facing apps on the hotpath experiencing increased token latency and 2 degraded requests/min errors. Noticable error surge started at 20:10Z. Please include that in the ticket.
Lee: Also enabling a temporary capacity fallback: route `hotpath` will also route to `us-west-dedicated` pool with throttling to limit burst — adding weight 10% to fallback. Applying policy now.
OpsBot: routing: added fallback target `us-west-dedicated` weight 10%.
Priya: For longer-term triage, I'll capture runtime version and model memory footprints. quick check: runtime v1.8.3 on the flapping nodes, model hot-13B uses ~28GB GPU mem when token buffer fills. If there's a memory leak, it would push it over 32GB and cause OOM.
Maya: reproducer command I'm running: ```stress-ng --gpu 1 --timeout 300s && run-runtime --model hot-13B --batch 32 --seq 1024``` — trying to reproduce the steady leak.
Anil: Cloud support replied: quota bump approved +8 gpus in 33m. Will post when completed.
Sam: Next actions list: 1) keep nodes cordoned, 2) maintain route throttles and fallback, 3) track quota increase, 4) debug runtime memory leak and rollback to previous runtime if necessary, 5) customer comms draft.
Lee: Implementation: throttles + fallback + max_concurrency applied. Observed immediate queue drop from 140 -> 70 in 2m. p95 latency down from 450ms -> 260ms.
Priya: While we debug, a safe short-term workaround may be to pin hot-13B to a quantized variant that uses less memory. That will lower quality slightly but improve stability.
Sam: Agreed. Lee, can you roll traffic to `hot-13B-qtz` with canary 20%?
Lee: initiating canary: `deploy hot-13B-qtz to hotpath 20%` — canary running. Monitoring.
IncidentBot: Note: page still active. Handing for on-call shift change at 21:00Z — @Anil will take follow-ups after 21:00Z.
Anil: I'll take post-21:00. Current status summary to paste in incidents channel and to include in support ticket: queue reduced, quota request pending, nodes cordoned, canary quantized model in flight, debugging runtime memory leak.
Maya: Uploading core dumps and heap traces to shared drive (link: https://redwood.internal/s/CLD-82492/dumps).
Sam: Thanks team. If quota doesn't land within 45m, we'll schedule a controlled rollback: either revert the runtime to v1.8.2 or expand fallback routing to 30%. Will update.
Priya: For postmortem: capture timeline, memory profiles, model footprints, and autoscaler behavior during node reset storms.
Lee: Noted. I'll leave throttles + fallback stable for the night unless we see regressions.
OpsBot: quota increase applied at 2026-03-10T20:46:10Z: +8 gpus. New effective pool capacity up in ~2m.
Sam: Confirming: pool capacity increased, scheduler placed 6 new nodes, queue drained to <10 within 4m. Observed 0 new node flaps after cordon.
Anil: leaving this in follow-up state for postmortem. Assigning owners: Maya (runtime triage), Priya (memory profiling), Lee (routing + rollback plan), Sam (postmortem and customer comms).
IncidentBot: incident severity downgraded to pg-2 at 2026-03-10T21:05:00Z. Paging stopped.
Sam: I'll prepare a short customer-facing note summarizing: transient capacity + runtime instability caused degraded latency for limited customers, mitigations applied (throttling, fallback, quota bump), root cause investigation ongoing.
Maya: logging out for now, will keep diagnostics running. if anything spikes ping in thread.
Anil: thanks everyone, leaving follow-up notes in ticket #CLD-82492 and creating the postmortem doc draft.
Priya: uploaded initial memory-profile diffs to the shared drive.
Lee: monitoring dashboards look stable. closing active pager monitor.
